episodes.title: What even is a Bitcoin block?
transcript: What even is a Bitcoin block?
Quick note: StarMiner sent me this miner.
Picture Bitcoin as one giant shared notebook.
Each page is a block: a batch of transactions.
About every ten minutes, the network adds a new page.
Miners race to seal it.
My little miner is in that race, page after page.
Solo mining does not guarantee rewards.
Follow for part two: what a miner actually does.

episodes.title: What does a Bitcoin miner actually do all day?
transcript: So what does a Bitcoin miner actually do all day?
Quick note: StarMiner sent me this one.
To add the next block, there's a puzzle to solve.
And the only way to solve it is to keep trying numbers.
Try, check, nope. Try, check, nope.
Miners everywhere do this nonstop, super fast.
While it's running, mine never stops trying.
Solo mining does not guarantee rewards.
Follow for part three: why it's called mining.

episodes.title: It's called Bitcoin mining. So where's the shovel?
transcript: It's called Bitcoin mining. So where's the shovel?
StarMiner sent me this one, and it doesn't dig.
Gold miners dig through rock to find something rare.
Bitcoin miners dig through numbers instead.
Whoever finds the next block gets new bitcoin as the reward.
That's the mining part. The digging is math.
And my little miner digs for every block.
Solo mining does not guarantee rewards.
Follow for more desk miner basics.

transcript: Setting up my miner, the app gave me one big choice.

Solo, you keep the whole block reward, but only if your miner finds the block itself.

episodes.title: Why a Bitcoin block about every 10 minutes?
transcript: Why does Bitcoin add a block about every ten minutes?
Quick note: StarMiner sent me this miner.
If more miners join, blocks would come faster.
So about every two weeks, the network checks its pace.
Too fast? The puzzle gets harder. Too slow? It gets easier.
That keeps it near ten minutes on average.
My little miner? It just keeps trying.
Solo mining does not guarantee rewards.
Follow for more desk miner basics.

episodes.title: What happens when a miner finds a block?
transcript: What actually happens when a miner finds a block?
Quick note: StarMiner sent me this miner.
First, it sends the new block out to the network.
Computers everywhere check it against the rules.
If it checks out, it's added, and the finder gets new bitcoin plus fees.
Then everyone starts over on the very next block.
Including my little miner.
Solo mining does not guarantee rewards.
Follow for more desk miner basics.

Pool: a team of miners sharing the work and the rewards.
Hashrate: how fast a miner can try.
Mine is tiny. The network is huge.
Solo mining does not guarantee rewards.

episodes.title: Why is it called a blockchain?
transcript: Why is it called a blockchain?
Quick note: StarMiner sent me this miner.
Each block stores the fingerprint of the one before it.
That links the blocks together into a chain.
Change an old block, and every link after it breaks.
That's why Bitcoin's history is so hard to rewrite.
My little miner tries to add the next link.
Solo mining does not guarantee rewards.
Follow for more honest desk miner basics.

My little miner keeps trying the next block.
Solo mining does not guarantee rewards.
